semantics.note: The claim keeps 'over 100', the books-and-articles scope and the one-database qualifier. It is a firm past-tense observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: at least 101 Marcus works that Meta acquired from LibGen without authorisation. Ruling out a catalog listing on its own as proof of acquisition is a reasonable reading of 'Meta pirated'.

evidence.note: The Kadrey opinion (June 2025, before the evaluation date) confirms that Meta torrented LibGen and trained on what it downloaded. It does not identify or count any Marcus works, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The general LibGen acquisition by Meta is established by the court record. Nothing in the packet independently verifies a list of at least 101 Marcus works, or matches them to what Meta actually downloaded. Nothing contradicts the count either, so the evidence does not settle it.
